items.title: #IDNWatch🇮🇩: Indonesia is experiencing nationwide blackouts as a result of coal shortages. At the heart of the crisis is a longstanding price control policy requiring miners to sell 25% of their production to domestic buyers at $70 per metric ton, a price well below current market levels. Rather than increasing coal supplies at home, the policy has encouraged some producers to pay non-compliance penalties instead of selling domestically. In 1998, when I was President Suharto’s chief economic advisor, I recommended abolishing price controls in Indonesia. If that advice had been taken, there would be no blackouts in Indonesia today.

items.content:
WHEN IT COMES TO THE BAB EL-MANDEB STRAIT, THE HOUTHIS RUN THE SHOW.

 x.com/windwardai/status/2087… Windward (@WindwardAI)12 Saudi-flagged tankers and bulkers are on the same route around the Cape of Good Hope right now. None through Bab el-Mandeb.
